# Ada Example's brain

Ada Example's private brain: the rules for every project, the backlog graph, the decision log, the journal and the
records, kept in git and read by the `brain` command at zero token. This repo is private: it stays in Ada Example's own
account or organisation.

## Install

The engine is the `brain` command, at the tag config.json `engine.pin` names (see the engine's install guide). Claude
Code gets the hooks, the guards and the injected rules from this folder, once:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add <this folder>
claude plugin install brain-core@brain
```

## Usage

```bash
brain status                                   # the backlog, the decisions waiting, the journal
brain item add wi-first --title "My first item" --priority P1
brain decision ask --title "..." --question "..." --option "A: ..." --option "B: ..." --why "..."
brain journal add --title "Today" "what was done"
brain tui                                      # the cockpit (brain tui --once: one text screen)
```

Edits to the backlog, the journal and the decisions go through these commands; the views (`notes/kanban_graph.md`,
`notes/roadmap_graph.md`, and the decision queue once a decision is asked) are regenerated by `brain sync`, never
edited by hand.

## Tests

`brain check` checks the graph, the records, the Claude rendering and the boundary (`boundary.yaml`): every tracked
file has a side, and the files that may be published one day (`src/`, `tests/`, `fixtures/`) hold nothing private.
